body.title: `issue view --comments` prints only the first page of notes, while `mr view --comments` reads them all
body.description:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: glab 1.124.0 (d43ccacec)
- [x] Operating system and version: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? gitlab.com
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues

### Summary

`glab issue view --comments` only prints the comments found in the first page of notes (20 notes by default, system notes included, oldest first), and gives no hint that more pages exist. On an issue with more than 20 notes, the most recent comments are silently missing.

`glab mr view --comments` does not have this problem: it reads every page of discussions. The two commands behave differently for the same flag.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.124.0 (d43ccacec)

Other: output redirected to a file (no TTY, no pager).

### Steps to reproduce

Issue #1165 of this project has 40 notes, 12 of which are comments; 2 of those comments come after the 20th note.

```shell
glab issue view 1165 -R gitlab-org/cli --comments | grep -c ' commented '
glab issue view 1165 -R gitlab-org/cli --comments --per-page 100 | grep -c ' commented '
glab issue view 1165 -R gitlab-org/cli --comments --output json \
  | jq '[.Notes[] | select(.system | not)] | length'
```

For comparison, merge request !4187 has 56 notes, 22 of which are comments or replies; only 5 of them are within the first 20 notes.

```shell
glab mr view 4187 -R gitlab-org/cli --comments | grep -cE '^ *@[^ ]+ (commented|replied) .*\[note #'
glab mr view 4187 -R gitlab-org/cli --comments --per-page 5 | grep -cE '^ *@[^ ]+ (commented|replied) .*\[note #'
glab mr view 4187 -R gitlab-org/cli --comments --page 2 | grep -cE '^ *@[^ ]+ (commented|replied) .*\[note #'
```

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

- `issue view --comments` prints 10 comments out of 12, while its own header says `comments: 12`. The JSON output has the same gap: `user_notes_count` is 12, but `Notes` holds only 10 non-system notes.
- With `--per-page 100`, all 12 comments are printed. An issue with more than 100 notes cannot be read in full in one call.
- `mr view --comments` prints all 22 comments, and still 22 with `--per-page 5`. However, `--page 2` sets the first page it reads and silently drops the oldest discussions: it prints 14 comments.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

`issue view --comments` prints every comment of the issue, as `mr view --comments` does. If paginated output is kept on purpose, the command should say that more notes exist and how to get them.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

Counts measured on 2026-10-26 with the commands above:

| Command | Comments printed | Comments on the issuable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue view 1165 --comments` | 10 | 12 |
| `issue view 1165 --comments --per-page 100` | 12 | 12 |
| `mr view 4187 --comments` | 22 | 22 |
| `mr view 4187 --comments --per-page 5` | 22 | 22 |
| `mr view 4187 --comments --page 2` | 14 | 22 |

### Possible fixes

- `internal/commands/issuable/view/issuable_view.go`: `listIssueNotes` calls `client.Notes.ListIssueNotes` once, with `PerPage` set to `api.DefaultListLimit` (20) when `--per-page` is not given. It could read every page, as `mrutils.ListAllDiscussions` does for `mr view` (`internal/commands/mr/view/mr_view.go`).
- On both commands, `--page` and `--per-page` could then be dropped or documented. Today they mean "read one page" on `issue view` and "start reading at this page" on `mr view`.

Related: #8051 covers comment management in general, not this pagination gap.

body.title: CI: fix lint cache save failing with no space left on device
body.description:
The `lint` job fails to save its cache:

```
FATAL: write ../../../cache/gitlab-org/cli/<hash>/archive_635336076: no space left on device
Failed to create cache
```

The cache being restored was last modified 2026-10-09, so `golangci-lint` analyses more each day as the cache goes staler (the lint step itself took 2m12s).

Options:
- Drop `.gocache` from lint's cache paths and keep only `.golangci-lint-cache` (lint's `.gocache` alone is about 127k files).
- Use a runner with more disk for the cache-saving `main` pipeline.

Pipeline: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/pipelines/2961140219

body.title: `glab ci view` shows stages in incorrect order
body.description:

Please read this!

Before opening a new issue, make sure to search for keywords in the issues

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/?label_name%5B%5D=type%3A%3Abug

and verify the issue you're about to submit isn't a duplicate.
--->

### Checklist

<!-- Please test the latest versions, that will remove the possibility that you see a bug that is fixed in a newer version. -->

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`) 
  - Extension version: glab 1.131.0 (206ebab4f)
- [x] Operating system and version: Debian 13
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) v19.4.8-ee
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [ ] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

<!-- Summarize the bug encountered concisely -->
For some pipelines, jobs and stages display in the incorrect order.

### Environment

<!--

on POSIX system (Linux, MacOS), run

bash -c 'printf -- "- OS: %s\n- SHELL: %s\n- TERM: %s\n- GLAB: %s" "$(uname -srm)" "$SHELL" "$TERM" "$(glab --version)"'

and replace the following section with the result.

If you use non-POSIX system, fill in the section manually:

- OS: Your operating system including version and architecture (Windows 11 - AMD64, MacOS Sonoma - ARM64)
- SHELL: Your shell (bash, fish, zsh, ...)
- TERM: Your terminal emulator (Kitty, Xterm2..)
- GLAB: result of running `glab --version` (glab version 1.32.0 (2023-08-18))

-->

- OS: Debian 13
- SHELL: bash
- TERM: Windows Terminal + tmux
- GLAB: glab 1.131.0 (206ebab4f)

<!--
Please include any other information that you believe might be relevant
in debugging. For example, you may include a shell framework like oh-my-zsh
or other customizations like editing the prompt (PS1, PS2, and others).
-->
Other:

### Steps to reproduce

<!-- How one can reproduce the issue - this is very important -->
Run `glab ci view`

The pipeline I frequently see this on has explicit dependencies between each plan and apply job pair (`needs: [job: "?_plan"]` on the apply jobs), which may or may not be triggering this incorrect behavior.

This also seems to happen most often (possibly always) on jobs that have or are being retried via the gitlab-ci.yml `retry:` directive.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

<!-- What actually happens -->

Some jobs and stages display in incorrect order. In addition, the jobs that are displayed incorrectly cannot be selected.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

<!-- What you should see instead -->
Jobs and stages should display in correct order

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

<!--- Paste the activity log from your command line -->
Incorrect view in `glab ci view`:

![image](/uploads/a99ca6f6be344afa0e3b4fee211b1bed/image.png){width=697 height=600}

The correct, equivalent view on the web UI:
![image](/uploads/0808a5280fe329bd7f07f99ff9056b6c/image.png){width=900 height=568}
